title: Regression analysis as a Wikipedia category node
dek: An encyclopedia family: mean maps, residuals, many named children. OLS/GLM plates already own the geometry you actually fit.
story: Wikipedia's Regression analysis article (and the category it sits in) is a family name: you are modelling E[Y | X] (or a quantile, or a robust location) as a function of covariates. Named children — OLS, GLM, logistic, Poisson, Cox, mixed models — already have Simplfy plates or sibling glossary cards.

The encyclopedia will happily mix predictive 'curve fitting' with causal 'effect of X'. This studio splits those: confounding/DAGs and potential outcomes are other plates. A regression category page is not a research design.
NIST remains definitional authority for least squares as a computational object. Wikipedia is the graph of names.
deep: Linearity can mean linear in parameters (OLS) or a linear predictor inside a link (GLM). Category pages blur that.
Regularisation (ridge/lasso) is a child with a bias–variance plate nearby.
Do not report a Wikipedia 'regression' as if it specified a likelihood.
TB-lab examples still live on the child plates (logit for R/S, Poisson for counts).

visual.caption: Category node, then children Simplfy already treats in depth, then the causal fork the encyclopedia often skips.
